PullRequest.Title: chat: add configurable GPT Live session awareness

## Summary

Add experimental `agents.voice.sessionAwareness` (enabled by default) so OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode receives a bounded briefing and can answer read-only session status questions without submitting coding work.

- Send revisioned snapshots of up to 20 tracked sessions, prioritizing the active session, with a 48,000-character serialized budget. Deduplicate unchanged snapshots and supersede old context on updates/removals.
- Include bounded titles, states, response summaries, and active-chat pending details, selected model, attachment names, and three recent turns. No attachment contents or background conversation history; exclude unfinished/canceled assistant text.
- Preserve actual background waiting-for-input state for aware GPT Live. Hosted voice and disabled-setting behavior remain unchanged.
- Keep coding work, navigation, corrections, and approvals/questions on existing client-controlled delegation. No new intent classifier or session-query tools.
- Keep awareness-enabled GPT Live connections silent until meaningful user speech or explicit application narration. Suppress unsolicited startup output and delegation so reconnect briefings do not replay old responses.
- Update Chat Accessibility Help. Disable the setting and reconnect to restore input-only context and clear the old briefing from the voice connection.

The first build found an outdated local Copilot SDK. `npm run install-fast` refreshed root dependencies but failed at a later registry-authentication step (E401); the subsequent full build and validation above succeeded. No registry configuration or credentials changed.

Live microphone/model behavior is not covered by deterministic tests. Full integration/smoke suites were not run.

## Manual testing

1. Open the Agents window, configure an accessible OpenAI live model in `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel`, and start Voice Mode in an existing chat.
2. With `agents.voice.sessionAwareness` enabled, ask “Where were we?”, “What just happened?”, and “Which tracked session needs input?”. Answers should use the briefing without creating coding requests.
3. Complete another turn and ask again. Verify updated context and no unsolicited briefing narration.
4. Verify coding requests and explicit approvals still delegate to the bound input and retain existing input-switch safety behavior.
5. Disable `agents.voice.sessionAwareness`, disconnect/reconnect Voice Mode, and verify input-only behavior returns.

6. With awareness enabled, hear a completed coding response, disconnect and reconnect, then remain silent. The old response must not replay; asking “What just happened?” should still work. A new coding completion or pending prompt may still be explicitly narrated.

Testing tracked in #343523.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added unconditional serializer call, the post-serialization deduplication, and the controller's subscription from response `onDidChange` to `_sendContext()` are explicit. `ChatResponseModel` forwards response value changes through `onDidChange`, so multiplicity tracks streaming updates. Exact response sizes and event rates vary, affecting severity but not the repeated-work mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: renderer CPU work and temporary arrays/strings created by history extraction, sorting, mapping, and JSON serialization
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is approximately O(D × (S log S + B + H)), where D is the number of response change events in a streamed turn, S is tracked sessions, B is the serialized briefing size (bounded at 48,000 characters), and H is the full markdown size joined before the 600-character per-turn cap.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased CPU/GC pressure and renderer latency during streamed responses
Findings.PreviousBehavior: GPT-Live context updates compared only the small active-session grounding and did not rebuild a full session briefing or recent conversation on each response change; explicit session-thread extraction happened only when that tool was requested.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: With awareness enabled by default, every context publication now rebuilds the complete bounded briefing before discovering that it is unchanged. The controller's reactive model path publishes context again for response `onDidChange` events, including ordinary streaming deltas where completed-only recent turns cannot change.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1515 adds `serializeGptLiveSessionBriefing(sessionContext)` to every GPT-Live `sendSessionContext` call, and the equality check is only performed after the complete snapshot has been sorted, mapped, JSON-stringified, and size-checked.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding the full briefing for every streamed response delta
Findings.Impact: While an agent streams a response during BYOK Voice Mode, each response chunk can synchronously rebuild an unchanged multi-session briefing on the renderer thread. Sessions with long prior markdown responses or a large tracked roster cause repeated CPU and temporary-string allocation, increasing GC pressure and risking delayed voice/UI responsiveness throughout generation.
Findings.Evidence: `voiceSessionController.ts` subscribes an autorun to `lastReq.response.onDidChange`; when a delta does not create a state transition, its `else` branch calls `_sendContext()`. That reaches this added line. `serializeGptLiveSessionBriefing` copies and sorts all tracked sessions, maps up to 20, and calls `JSON.stringify`; `getVoiceRecentTurns`, also newly attached to the active context, filters/maps/joins all markdown for up to three completed responses before slicing each assistant string to 600 characters. During an in-progress response, those completed turns and the briefing normally remain unchanged, but all of this allocation occurs before `briefing !== this._gptLiveBriefing` suppresses the send.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep immediate active-input grounding, but coalesce or gate briefing reconstruction on meaningful roster/state/pending/focus/completed-turn revisions rather than raw response deltas. Cache the bounded recent-turn representation per completed request, and stop collecting markdown once the 600-character limit is reached so discarded text is never joined.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect or reconnect OpenAI BYOK Voice Mode with session awareness enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the OpenAI live session and WebRTC channel connect, `sendStartSession` synchronously sends instructions and the initial context before the session-init microtask. Briefing construction and all data-channel sends are therefore on initialization's renderer-thread path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the OpenAI GPT-Live WebRTC session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One OpenAI session-creation request remains per connection. The new initial briefing is one logical snapshot split into roughly ceil((prefix + serialized briefing UTF-8 bytes)/500) data-channel sends; the briefing itself is capped at 48,000 characters and 20 sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session-creation request was required before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The HTTP request establishes the session as before. The new synchronous serialization and data-channel burst run before session initialization is announced locally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append the initial session briefing over the RTC data channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial awareness snapshot, chunked into 500-byte events; exact chunk count depends on escaped content and UTF-8 width.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GPT-Live sent only language/current-input grounding here, generally a small event, and no roster/recent-turn briefing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds synchronous renderer work and outbound WebRTC events during GPT-Live startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tracked sessions (all sorted, up to 20 serialized), bounded field lengths, JSON escaping, and UTF-8 byte width.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialization and 500-byte `RTCDataChannel.send` calls are synchronous and sequential; there is no limiter or coalescer for the initial snapshot.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first context always serializes and sends a briefing. `_gptLiveBriefing` deduplicates identical snapshots only after serialization; reconnect/disconnect clears it, so each connection is cold. No recent-turn extraction cache exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the serializer, 500-byte chunk loop, and call order are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical briefing size and tracked-session count vary; the cap bounds each startup burst, so this startup cost alone was not reported separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: The new bounded startup work is intentional and finite. It contributes to the reported hot-path design but is not independently severe enough for another finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep Voice Mode connected while the coding agent streams a response
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat response `onDidChange` invalidates the controller autorun. Non-transition streaming deltas call `_sendContext`, which synchronously builds recent turns and serializes the full briefing on the renderer thread. Only after that can equality suppress the network send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send changed session-briefing revisions over the WebRTC data channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For unchanged streaming deltas, zero data-channel calls after deduplication, but one full briefing serialization per delta. For meaningful roster/state/completed-turn changes, one full briefing is split into 500-byte sequential sends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Streaming context publications performed only small active-grounding comparisons; they did not construct a full briefing, and outbound grounding changed only with the active input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repeated local work competes with UI and voice event handling during generation; changed snapshots also synchronously enqueue the outbound chunks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or load an unloaded chat model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A needs-input unloaded session can trigger at most one guarded `acquireOrLoadSession` per session while a load is in flight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same load was already triggered for unloaded needs-input sessions before state scoping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Loading is asynchronous and supports pending-state narration; it is not caused or made more frequent by the awareness changes reviewed here.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Response delta count multiplied by tracked-session snapshot size and full markdown size of up to three recent completed turns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates execute serially on the UI event loop. There is state-transition settling, but the autorun's no-transition branch publishes immediately for ordinary response deltas; there is no awareness-specific debounce before serialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact serialized briefing equality prevents WebRTC sends for unchanged contexts, but the cache is consulted only after rebuilding the snapshot. Completed recent turns are recomputed from model responses on every publication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: response changes explicitly feed `_sendContext`, completed-only history remains stable while streaming, and equality occurs after serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Streaming event rate and historical markdown sizes vary by provider and task, so exact frame/latency impact is workload-dependent; the per-delta repeated mechanism is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: default-enabled awareness repeatedly rebuilds an unchanged snapshot on a hot response-delta path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Tracked sessions start, complete, request input, or change focus during a long voice connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Settled agent state, pending-detail, focus, roster, and completed-summary changes rebuild context before narration. Some paths explicitly flush because narration validation depends on current context.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append a revisioned complete session snapshot to GPT Live.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete briefing per effective changed snapshot, split into 500-byte RTC messages; changes are coalesced at the controller's state-settle boundary but not encoded as deltas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only active-input grounding was appended when its compact id/label/state/pending-type tuple changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Context must be published before associated narration can proceed on flush paths, so the outbound burst can precede narration progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective changed state/roster/focus/completed-turn revisions and serialized snapshot byte size after session and field caps.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: State-transition storms are settled in the controller, then a full snapshot is serialized and RTC chunks are sent sequentially. Periodic polling itself sends only when it detects a state change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A changed serialized snapshot advances `_gptLiveBriefingRevision`; identical snapshots are suppressed. There is no delta encoding, so every meaningful change sends the complete bounded roster.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the full-snapshot sends and ordering; remote model retention semantics for appended revisions are not established by repository evidence and were not treated as a finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Realistic rosters are often below the 20-session/48,000-character caps, and state settling reduces bursts. Without measured model/session duration, full-snapshot boundary fan-out was not reported separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: Bounded but potentially sizable network fan-out is introduced. Evidence is insufficient for a separate high-confidence user-visible regression beyond the reported repeated local reconstruction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ask for explicit session-thread information through the existing voice tool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit voice tool waits for session information, then its JSON result is returned through the existing GPT-Live delegation/data-channel path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return bounded recent session turns through the existing delegation flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing delegated tool result per explicit session-info request, subsequently chunked by the existing GPT-Live append helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same last-N extraction and JSON response occurred inline before the helper extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The result is required before the voice model can answer that explicit tool request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit tool-call frequency, requested last-N count, and markdown response size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One dispatch runs per delegated tool call; no new parallel fan-out was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The helper reads only the last requested count of turns. The refactored explicit session-info path has the same lack of caching and the same output bounds as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff is a direct helper extraction with equivalent default behavior when `completedResponsesOnly` is false.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Assistant markdown can be large, but invocation frequency and output behavior on this explicit path are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-introduced performance regression; behavior is equivalent to the prior inline implementation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remain silent after awareness-enabled connection or reconnect, then speak or request narration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Inbound transcript/delegation events are checked before output handling. Muting changes playback gain/HTML audio state but does not add filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, or HTTP work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive GPT-Live audio, transcript, and delegation events over WebRTC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing continuous inbound WebRTC audio/events; no additional outbound event is sent merely because unsolicited output is suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same inbound stream existed, but output was not held silent for awareness startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The checks are constant-time and keep unsolicited output off the playback path until speech or requested narration.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: WebRTC event callbacks remain event-loop serialized; no new worker, queue, or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Awaiting-first-interaction is connection-local state and resets on disconnect. No extra audio buffers or retained collections are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed branches only gate existing event processing and audio mute state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Live microphone/model timing is inherently environment-dependent, but the added state checks are constant-time.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the added checks are constant-time and introduce no retained-resource growth or new boundary calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files. One medium repeated-work regression was reported: full awareness snapshots and recent history are reconstructed for every streamed response delta before deduplication. Startup, changed-snapshot RTC fan-out, explicit thread retrieval, model loading, and first-interaction audio gating were traced separately; no additional issue met the high-confidence performance threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
